solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drink trade with damned new market force

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips
to ply a trade is to work at it
and means together with

indicators.note: new says the letters of damned are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A drinks seller cursing some damned new competitor in the market.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'damned new' as a curse on a rival, but 'new' is the signal to reshuffle the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The economists' phrase names the twin pressures that set prices in any market.

clue.text: Stayed at home making glossy material

parts.note: sat means remained seated, stayed put
in means at home, not out

explanation.surface: Someone who stayed in, sewing with shiny fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: This smooth silk-type fabric is prized for its lustrous sheen.

clue.text: Dot over "i" — what may be found in pizza and deli, say

definitions.text: what may be found in pizza and deli, say

parts.note: to pepper is to dot or sprinkle all over
on means over, upon

explanation.surface: A pedantic note about dotting an i, then a hint about food.
explanation.definitionFit: This spicy sausage appears as a pizza topping and in delicatessen counters.

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: A tardy pupil is sent to detention or locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' suggests imprisonment but means eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held up arrives behind time, a straight synonym.

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: airs means puts on the radio or television
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A rock radio show playing Led Zeppelin over a shared spliff.
explanation.walkthrough: Led Zeppelin the band tempts, but a Zeppelin is also a German dirigible.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeppelins were rigid dirigibles, an example of the lighter-than-air craft.

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
U is the old label for upper-class usage
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A titled lady leaves after a posh board game.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke's wife holds this rank in the peerage, a noble lady.

indicators.note: ingredients (misspelt as printed) are parts to be mixed, so the letters are stirred together anew

explanation.surface: Separate the ingredients for a festive present, misspellings and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ingerdients' and 'seasonl' are typos as printed; the jumbled 'ingredients' is itself a playful mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate eggs are the traditional present at the spring Christian festival.

indicators.note: short asks for the word Roman with its final letter cut off

parts.note: a citizen of Rome

explanation.surface: A description of a classic aquiline profile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nose' looks like the facial feature but is the sense of smell's object.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose in wine-tasting is a smell or bouquet, a scent.

clue.text: Rare Fender, if electric, beginning to tempt

indicators.note: electric suggests a jolt that sets these letters jumping into a new order
beginning to asks for just the opening letter

explanation.surface: A rare electric Fender guitar starts to tempt a collector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'electric' rearranges FENDER IF into DIFFEREN; T, the first of 'tempt', ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare or unusual is out of the ordinary, unlike the rest.

clue.text: At wit's end priest rouses one napping?

indicators.note: wit's end asks for the last letter of wit

parts.note: the possessive points to the word wit

indicators.note: rouses suggests stirring the letters of priest into a new order

explanation.surface: A desperate cleric shakes awake someone dozing.
explanation.walkthrough: A nap in racing is a tipster's best bet, so napping means tipping, not dozing.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing slang a nap is a confident tip, so a nap-giver makes predictions.

clue.text: Who's ejected from clubs like a Hooray Henry?

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
as means like
a Hooray Henry is a loud upper-class young man, a toff

explanation.surface: A rowdy posh boy thrown out of nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: A Hooray Henry is British slang for a braying upper-class young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A discarded person or thing, rejected by others, is thrown aside.

clue.text: Want a part of fine education

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wishing for a share of a good schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: To want is to lack or require, a straight synonym.

definitions.meaning: slang for glamour photographs of attractive people
a creamy dessert, one example of a sweet course

explanation.surface: Something lovely to look at is perhaps sugary too.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both pin-up photography and a baked dessert with a cream filling.

parts.note: to own up is to confess, come clean

explanation.surface: A mature Greek finally confesses.
explanation.definitionFit: A fully mature person, no longer a child, as a noun.

clue.text: Carve up roast in good British eatery

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters between the two outer pieces
to carve is to cut into pieces, so the letters are sliced and rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to carve the Sunday joint in a fine British restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carve' looks like a kitchen instruction but signals reshuffling; 'in' puts the result between the two single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub serving restaurant-quality food is a place to dine, an eating house.

clue.text: Tend to help maiden first — I do

definitions.text: Tend to help maiden first — I do

indicators.note: first puts the maiden's letter before that for help

parts.note: to nurse is to tend or care for
M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over
aid means help

explanation.surface: A carer says that tending the young girl comes first.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, written M.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue is the job description: someone employed to look after young children.

indicators.note: changes says the letters of respect are rearranged

explanation.surface: Losing respect alters how one is seen for the worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostly apparition, or a looming threat, is a frightening picture in the mind.

clue.text: So free her to form a new group

indicators.note: the three words regroup into a new arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Liberate a woman so she can start her own band.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words introduce a conclusion, meaning consequently.

indicators.note: retains means holds inside

parts.note: to stir up is to kindle or provoke

indicators.note: primary asks for the first letter

explanation.surface: An Amazon e-reader keeps a bookseller's main market grip.
explanation.walkthrough: Kindle looks like the e-reader; it means stir up, which keeps R from 'retailer's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider's foot rests in this loop hanging from the saddle.

parts.note: to patter is to talk rapidly and smoothly

explanation.surface: A smooth talker then names a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A template or example to copy, as in a dressmaker's guide.

indicators.note: ground means crushed to powder, so the letters are broken up and remixed

parts.note: the spice name, with the apostrophe s acting as is

explanation.surface: Grated spice makes the cake rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to increase or enlarge, a straight synonym.

indicators.note: leaves means departs from, so those two letters are taken out

parts.note: heartless means cold, unfeeling

explanation.surface: Frank is a cold man who walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank reads as a man's name but means candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being naive and without guile, someone is candid and open.

clue.text: For land and property etc redraft a letter with SAE

indicators.note: to redraft is to rewrite, so the letters are set down in a new order

explanation.surface: Rewrite a letter to an estate agent, enclosing a stamped addressed envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: SAE is the British stamped addressed envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Land and buildings together form immovable property in law.

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece is over the next
changed says the letters of bail are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A defendant offers a defence when bail is altered.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim of being elsewhere serves as a defence or justification.

parts.note: wee is Scots for small

explanation.surface: Is little Penny overweight?
explanation.walkthrough: Blubber reads as fat but is the verb to cry.
explanation.definitionFit: To blubber is to sob noisily, to cry.

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
arty means artistic and bohemian

explanation.surface: A subdued gathering of artistic types.
explanation.definitionFit: A social gathering or celebration, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Tender loving care includes a body treatment

indicators.note: includes means holds inside

explanation.surface: A spa's caring service comes with a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Powder dusted on the skin after bathing is a cosmetic for the body.

clue.text: Archbishop's affectedly proper answer leads to Times' editorial

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper

indicators.note: leads to asks for the first letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A prissy archbishop responds via a Times leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior archbishop of a country holds this title in church hierarchy.

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a mane is a mass of locks of hair

explanation.surface: Hair surrounding the doorway to our house.
explanation.walkthrough: Entrance is the verb to enchant, not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to charm and captivate them, make them fall in love.

clue.text: Co-op financier doing this strengthens companionship

definitions.meaning: a mutual savings and mortgage lender owned by its members
the phrase read literally: constructing fellowship

explanation.surface: A mutual lender boasts that its work builds fellowship.
explanation.definitionFit: A British mutual lender for home loans; read literally, it means forging fellowship.
